items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Your next phone could cost you more, and you're already paying for it. Its memory chip costs about three times January's price. Who's buying?
The chip is RAM, your device's short-term memory. TrendForce says contract prices jumped eighty percent in spring, forty percent in summer, and another twenty percent is coming.
So who's buying up all the memory?
A.I. Data centres running chatbots need mountains of memory, and they pay more than phone makers.
So chipmakers shift their factories to A.I. memory, and less is left for your laptop.
And that's not even the weirdest part.
In a way, the free chatbot on your phone is helping push up the price of your phone.
A.I. felt free. You just pay for it at the checkout.
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched banknote, worried] Can I pay in gigabytes?
Comment: would you pay more for A.I. in your phone?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
